content.text: {"label":"marketing_campaign","explanation":"General volume is running +58% to +82% above forecast every interval. The excess comes almost entirely from new_offer_enquiry: 140 calls against 15.3 expected (9.2x normal), now 34% of the mix against a usual 6%. This matches the 10:50 regional TV spot for the zero-balance savings account (2M audience, toll-free number on screen). Supply is not the problem: absences are normal, AHT is at or below forecast, and the only open incident is a P4 staff-email issue with no customer impact. General service level has been near 100% since 15:15 only because of the overtime and other levers already in place. The last overtime block and the chat deflection have just ended (16:00 and 16:15), while volume is still about 58% above forecast. Payments is stable at about 100% service level with volume close to forecast.","plan_name":"Sustain general cover after campaign levers expire","rationale":"The demand surge on general is continuing, but the capacity added earlier is falling away now. The plan restores that cover through to the end of the day. Chat deflection is restarted on the campaign-driven reasons to remove part of the excess calls. A new overtime offer covers 16:45-18:45, plus a smaller one to 20:00. Overtime spent so far is about Rs 8,640 if roughly 40% accepted, and these offers add about Rs 4,300, which stays within the Rs 15,000 budget. Until the overtime agents arrive at 16:45, four cross-skilled payments agents and a short break delay bridge the gap. Payments is well above 70% service level, so it can lend agents safely. Cancelling coaching adds cheap extra capacity.
